questions.prompt: Field Summary outputs three anchors. Which mapping is correct?
options: O = summary dataset for downstream · R = static written report · I = interactive profiling dashboard
O = chart · R = raw data · I = errors
O = output file · R = rerun · I = input
questions.explain: **O** feeds further workflow (rows = fields, cols = stats), **R** = static report for documentation/Render, **I** = the interactive dashboard you Browse for EDA. The drill's reading: UnitPrice may have mild outliers.

questions.prompt: Match: correlation between Age and MonthlyIncome → ? · counts per Gender → ? · Gender × Region joint counts → ?
options: Association Analysis (Pearson) · Frequency Table · Contingency Table
Plot of Means · Field Summary · Union
questions.explain: **Association Analysis** = correlation matrix (tick a target for detail); **Frequency Table** = one categorical's counts; **Contingency Table** = two categoricals crossed; **Plot of Means** = averages of a measure per group; **Scatterplot** = two numerics.

questions.prompt: Before TS Plot / ETS / ARIMA, the data must be:
options: Aggregated to EXACTLY ONE observation per period (Summarize: GroupBy month, Sum measure)
questions.explain: Time-series tools demand **one row per period** — hence Summarize (GroupBy OrderDate-by-month + Sum TotalSales). ETS and ARIMA are then both fed from that same stream, named models each.

options: L = the unioned model objects (ETS O + ARIMA O) · R = HOLDOUT data (most recent 10–20% of periods, withheld from training)
L = raw data · R = a chart
Both inputs are the full dataset
questions.explain: Models (via **Union**) into L; the **holdout** (last 10–20% of periods — slide-exact figure) into R. Metrics: **MAPE, RMSE, MAE, MASE — lower is better**. Winner's O → TS Forecast (95 + 80 intervals, 6 periods).

questions.prompt: The standard supervised pipeline order is:
options: Create Samples (70 E / 30 V) → model on E → (Stepwise refine) → Score with D = V data, M = model
Model on ALL data → evaluate on the same data
questions.explain: **Estimation/Validation split first** (anchors E/V/H), train on E, refine with **Stepwise** (direction Both, fit measure **AICc** — 'recommended for small datasets', keep MINIMUM AIC), then **Score**: D input = V rows, M input = model O. R anchor shows coefficients/p-values/R².

questions.prompt: Response = 1 is rare in the mailing data. Before logistic regression, the lab's fix is:
options: Oversample Field — field Response, level 1, percentage ≈ 50
questions.explain: **Oversample Field** rebalances the minority class for training. Note the original response rate FIRST (Frequency Table) — the Lift Chart later needs that **true response rate**; good lift = 'top 2 deciles capture most responders'.

questions.prompt: To rank Logistic/Decision Tree/Forest/Neural Net on validation data, you:
options: Union the four model O anchors → Model Comparison (M = models, D = V rows) → read the E anchor's error table (Accuracy, AUC, F1)
questions.explain: **Union models → Model Comparison**: E = error-measure scoreboard, P = actual-vs-predicted, R = diagnostic plots. Forest beats a single tree because bootstrapped trees + limited variables per split **reduce overfitting**.

questions.prompt: Customer segmentation with UNKNOWN K: the correct tool order is:
options: K-Centroids Diagnostics (test K range, z-score standardize) → K-Centroids Cluster Analysis (K from diagnostics) → Append Cluster → Summarize per cluster
questions.explain: Unsupervised (no target given): **Diagnostics** picks K (adjusted-Rand/CH indices peak), **Cluster Analysis** builds the solution (z-score, K-Means), **Append Cluster** labels every record (no config needed — slide-verbatim), then Summarize Avg per cluster to NAME the segments ('young high-spenders'…). Exclude Customer_ID from the fields!
